subject: Clarifying hosting responsibility matrix for Brightwell private pilot
messages:
From: Ryan Miller <ryan.miller@brightwell.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily@atlascloud.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Brightwell interest in private hosting + clarifying responsibilities

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Brightwell's security team is very interested in a VPC/private deployment for our ML inference (PHI-adjacent). Before we get deeper into procurement, they asked for a simple RACI: who owns the network landing zone, who builds/maintains the private control plane, and who is the escalation path for runtime issues.

We also want clarity on what Redwood will include in the pilot vs. what Brightwell must provide (network, HA, backup). Emily from AtlasCloud (our integrator) is on the thread to help map gaps. Can you point us to the right owners at Redwood so we can align expectations?

High-level asks from Brightwell:
- Runbook ownership for incident response (who is first-line)
- Audit log delivery cadence and format (they need weekly extracts for now)
- Pilot scope (minimal success criteria and timeline)

Appreciate a quick call if it's easier.

—Ryan
Director of Infrastructure
Brightwell Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Miller <ryan.miller@brightwell.health>
Cc: Emily Park <emily@atlascloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Brightwell interest in private hosting + clarifying responsibilities

Thanks, Ryan — looping in a few folks so we can be concrete.

Karthik: can you confirm technical ownership split (network landing zone, private control plane, runtime ops) and a realistic pilot timeline?
Grace: can you outline the ops/resourcing expectations (oncall, runbooks, monitoring handoffs) and whether we need a temporary support SLA for the pilot?
Monica: product/contracting — can you note procurement/Docs signoffs we should expect from Brightwell and any standard pilot terms?

If helpful, I can host a 30-minute sync tomorrow. For now, quick bullet answers in thread will be helpful — Brightwell wants a clear single-page RACI to circulate to their security team.

Thanks all,

—Steph
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Miller <ryan.miller@brightwell.health>, Emily Park <emily@atlascloud.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Brightwell interest in private hosting + clarifying responsibilities

On Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 10:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik: can you confirm technical ownership split (network landing zone, private control plane, runtime ops) and a realistic pilot timeline?

Quick take from infra/arch:
- Network landing zone: responsibility split. Brightwell/Atlas provides VPC peering details and firewall policy; Redwood provides a reference Terraform module and validates connectivity during onboarding. We do NOT provision customer VPC subnets — customer-owned.
- Private control plane: Redwood owns the control plane components we ship (agents, management API) in-customer VPC (multi-tenant control plane is not an option for this pilot). We will require a small management subnet and a service account with limited IAM scope.
- Runtime ops (inference runtime): Redwood owns model runtime binary, kernel/quantization selection, and token-serving logic. Brightwell owns node baseline OS patching & k8s cluster ops unless they contract Redwood Dedicated Ops add-on.

Pilot timeline (best effort):
- Week 0–1: NDA/Docs + network preflight (security questionnaire + firewall rules)
- Week 2: control plane deploy & basic smoke tests (we'll use a canary model)
- Week 3–4: full load tests, KV cache validation, and runbook handoff

Risks/notes:
- SOC / audit log delivery: we can push logs to an S3 bucket / GCS with a defined schema, but weekly extracts will be an additional integration task (ETA depends on Brightwell infra availability).
- Oncall: we can provide a 9–5 Redwood triage window during pilot. 24/7 support requires a paid SLA and staffing commitment.

I attached a draft RACI I used for prior pilots (hosting_ownership-RACI.xlsx) — feel free to adapt.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: hosting_ownership-RACI.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Miller <ryan.miller@brightwell.health>, Emily Park <emily@atlascloud.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Brightwell interest in private hosting + clarifying responsibilities

Thanks — adding ops perspective.

Operational asks we need to confirm for pilot:
- Runbooks: Redwood will supply runbooks for common incidents (deploy rollback, KV cache corruption, OOM). We expect Brightwell to host runbook copies in their knowledge base and follow their incident comms templates.
- Monitoring: Redwood will ship telemetry to a customer-facing metrics endpoint; Brightwell must provide access control for viewing. For escalation, Redwood L2 can triage during 9–5 PST; after-hours escalations will require Brightwell on-call unless they subscribe to 24/7 ops.
- Backup & retention: We recommend a short retention window for pilot (14 days) to reduce storage and preserve PII isolation. If Brightwell requires longer retention, we need to scope additional compliance work.

Staffing: expect 1 SRE (10% FTE) from Redwood for pilot coordination + 2 platform engineers (customer side) for network and cluster work during Week 0–2.

Pilot success criteria (proposed):
- Control plane deployed and successfully serves >= 95% of test requests under expected traffic pattern for 48h load test
- Audit logs delivered weekly in agreed schema
- Clear runbook acceptance and a documented handoff meeting

Drive doc with suggested pilot scope and resource checklist: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-hosting-raci (internal editable).

—Grace
Head of Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Miller <ryan.miller@brightwell.health>, Emily Park <emily@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Brightwell interest in private hosting + clarifying responsibilities

Ryan / Emily — thanks for the quick context and for being flexible. To summarize and make this actionable:

Decisions / ownership (pilot):
- Network landing zone: Brightwell/Atlas to provide VPC connectivity and firewall policy; Redwood provides TF module + validation (owner: Brightwell / Atlas).
- Private control plane: Redwood will deploy and manage control plane components inside Brightwell VPC for the pilot (owner: Redwood).
- Runtime ops: Redwood responsible for runtime binaries and token serving; Brightwell responsible for node/k8s platform maintenance unless opting for Redwood Dedicated Ops add-on.
- Audit logs: delivered weekly to an S3-compatible bucket (owner: Redwood to push; Brightwell to provide bucket and access).

Pilot next steps (owners & deadlines):
- Monica (Product) to produce a one-page pilot SOW and send to Brightwell for signature by 2025-03-18 — includes acceptance criteria & limited SLA.
- Karthik (Infra) to run control plane preflight checklist and share a deployment runbook by 2025-03-20.
- Grace (SRE) to confirm oncall coverage (9–5) and required Brightwell FTE by 2025-03-17.
- Ryan/Emily to confirm VPC details and open required firewall rules by 2025-03-17.

Attachments: I attached a short pilot scope doc (pilot-scope.pdf) for Monica to adapt. Monica — please add procurement/Docusign link and I'll route internally for approval.

If these owners/deadlines look good, we'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff next week.

—Steph
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot-scope.pdf (application/pdf)
body_summary: Cross-functional thread to define ownership split and pilot scope for Brightwell Health private (VPC) deployment. Agreed: Brightwell provides VPC and firewall, Redwood deploys control plane and runtime; audit logs to S3. Next steps assigned to Monica (SOW), Karthik (preflight/runbook), Grace (oncall), and Brightwell for network details.
